headline: 逐帧逆向网站动画的 Claude Code skill
summary_md:
**What it is.** Reanimate (NiazMorshed2007/reanimate) is a Claude Code skill that records an animation — from a live URL, screen recording, MP4, GIF or Lottie file — rebuilds it in your project's own stack, then films the rebuild the same way and compares the two until the numbers line up.

**Why it's taking off.** Agents usually recreate an animation in one pass and stop, because they can't see motion or measure how far off they are. Reanimate closes that loop: fixed-viewport headless capture, a per-element spec table (trigger, duration, from → to, easing, stagger), then 2–5 verify rounds with a real pixel/timing diff. The README shows 417/417 frames identical on a Vercel Toolbar clone, and a WebGPU ocean at 0 px difference over 12 seconds. It's MIT-licensed, needs no API keys, and the demo sites (Stripe, Clerk, Linear-adjacent) are exactly the animations devs already want.

**Where the product opportunity is.** Today it's a skill script, not a product. A hosted version — paste a link or drop a recording, pick a target (CSS, Framer Motion, GSAP, three.js), get code plus a side-by-side proof video — would make it usable by designers and coding-in-public founders who don't run Claude Code. Other plausible hooks: a paid preset library of hand-verified clones, a regression check that flags when your hero animation drifts after a CSS change, and a Figma/Webflow export path. The install weight (~250 MB of ffmpeg + Playwright Chromium on first run) and the Claude Code + Bun requirement are the main reasons a wrapper adds real value rather than just polish.
tagline_en: A Claude Code skill that clones animations from any site or video and proves the match frame by frame.
